bc_rocky_horror_wall.blurb: Rocky Horror Wall is a compact sport wall inside Cougar Canyon, in Kalamalka Lake Provincial Park near Vernon. It has five bolted routes and every one sits in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers who are comfortable at that level and want moderate lines without stepping up to harder ground. The gneiss in this canyon has a rough, textured feel. The wall sits just around a corner from the harder Beta Wall, and a path that trends downhill from the base of that wall leads across to it.

bc_bat_wall_2.blurb: Bat Wall is a small crag in Cougar Canyon, near Vernon in the Okanagan. It holds five routes, four of them sport and one trad, with grades running from easy 5.5 up to 5.10. The main wall is slabby and technical, the kind of climbing where footwork and working out the sequence matter more than strength, while the tower on the right side leans out. The canyon's gneiss is grainy and textured. A short scree trail and a few steps lead to a small belay area at the base.

bc_cedar_dome.blurb: Cedar Dome is a small, south-facing crag in Cougar Canyon near Vernon, tucked among trees and out of the wind. It has five sport routes, from 5.8 and a pair of 5.9s up to two at 5.11, and the face is marked by pockets and hueco-style holds that are unusual for the canyon. The grainy gneiss and the gentler grades at the bottom end make it a reasonable place for newer leaders to start, with a couple of harder lines for a later visit. It is a short walk beyond Toad Hall.

bc_raven_s_wall.blurb: Raven's Wall is an out-of-the-way crag at the rim end of Cougar Canyon, near Vernon. It has five routes, three sport and two trad, with grades from 5.7 to 5.11. The wall sees few visitors and was still being cleaned up recently, so expect some dirt and loose debris on the lines. The walk follows the canyon rim past Cougar Arete and Gray Wall, then drops down a gully and doubles back to the base.

bc_mourning_time.blurb: Mourning Time is a seldom-visited crag in the Maternal Group at Skaha Bluffs, near Penticton. It continues on from Screeching Wall to the north. It has five routes, four sport and one trad, nearly all in the 5.10 range with a single 5.11. Pitches run fairly long, and the sport lines make a short session for anyone who wants to get away from the weekend crowds. There is no tree shade at the base.

bc_the_outpost.blurb: The Outpost is a multipitch sport area in Cheakamus Canyon, in the Sea to Sky corridor near Squamish. It has five bolted routes of roughly three to six pitches each, graded from 5.9 to 5.11, with most around 5.10. The routes are well bolted and the crag looks across to the Tantalus Range. It lies away from the main Cheakamus crags and takes a real walk from the road, so it is a fuller day than a quick crag visit. Rockfall is possible, and a helmet is a sensible choice here.

bc_upper_tier_left.blurb: Upper Tier Left is a small section of the Road Rage crag beside Highway 99 in the Sea to Sky corridor, north of Squamish. It has five routes, three sport and two trad, falling between 5.10 and 5.11. The rock is steep and clean, set among trees, and it dries quickly after rain. The base is reached by walking up past the Lower Tier and bearing left, with the arete of Cartoon Physics making a handy landmark. It suits climbers working at the 5.10 to low 5.11 level who want a short, concentrated visit.
